summary_html: **Educators/school staff** observing indicators of abuse/neglect report to CPS under state mandatory-reporter lists built on the federal CAPTA floor.
authority_html: - **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — requires robust reporter regimes that include education sector professionals

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Doe-3 v. McLean County Unit District No. 5 Board of Directors
key_cases.holding: The court held school officials owed no affirmative common-law duty to warn or report, but that plaintiffs stated a willful and wanton claim based on defendants' alleged misrepresentation of a teacher's record to a subsequent employer, and remanded for further proceedings.
key_cases.relevance: The leading Illinois authority on educator responsibility when school staff learn of suspected abuse by a colleague.
key_cases.quote: the common law does not recognize an affirmative duty to act for the protection of another in the absence of a special relationship between the parties

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed denial of qualified immunity, holding that a caseworker's under-the-clothes examination of children at a private school exceeded the principal's consent to interview them and violated their clearly established Fourth Amendment rights.
key_cases.relevance: Governs child-protection interviews and examinations conducted on private school premises in this circuit.
key_cases.quote: the searches of the children's bodies to investigate child abuse were presumptively unreasonable, unless they fall within an exception to the warrant requirement of the Fourth Amendment

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed summary judgment for the caseworker defendants, holding the parents had not shown racial animus and that their equal protection and section 1985(3) conspiracy claims arising from a disabled child's removal therefore failed.
key_cases.relevance: The investigation began with a referral from school personnel who observed the child's condition.
key_cases.quote: To establish "purpose" under prong two, a plaintiff must demonstrate racial, ethnic, or other class-based "invidiously discriminatory animus behind the conspirators' actions."

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that caseworkers who searched a private religious school and seized a student for a child-abuse interview without a warrant, court order, probable cause, consent or exigent circumstances violated the Fourth Amendment and the family's right to familial relations, but affirmed qualified immunity because those rights were not yet clearly established.
key_cases.relevance: The foundational Seventh Circuit decision on child-abuse investigations conducted on private school premises without parental notice or consent.
key_cases.quote: although child welfare caseworkers may investigate allegations of child abuse without violating parents' constitutional right to familial relations, they may not do so arbitrarily

search_keywords: Illinois Department of Children and Family Services

state_agency.name: Illinois Department of Children and Family Services

mandatory_reporters: Medical personnel — physicians, residents, interns, psychiatrists, surgeons, dentists, dental hygienists, chiropractic and podiatric physicians, physician assistants, emergency medical technicians, physical and occupational therapists, acupuncturists, registered/licensed practical/advanced practice nurses, genetic counselors, respiratory care practitioners, home health aides, certified nursing assistants — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(1)

Social services and mental health personnel — licensed counselors, social workers, psychologists, marriage and family therapists, field personnel of Healthcare and Family Services, Public Health, Human Services, Human Rights and DCFS, General Assistance supervisors/administrators, social services administrators, substance abuse treatment personnel — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(2)
Crisis intervention personnel — crisis line or hotline personnel, domestic violence program personnel — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(3)

Education personnel — school personnel (administrators, certified and non-certified employees), personnel of institutions of higher education, educational advocates, school board members (to the extent required by subsection (d)), truant officers — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(4)
Recreation or athletic program or facility personnel; athletic trainers — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(5)
Child care personnel — early intervention providers, nursery school and early care and education center directors and staff, foster parents, homemakers, child care workers — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(6)

Law enforcement personnel — law enforcement officers, Department of Juvenile Justice and Department of Corrections field personnel, probation officers, animal control officers and Department of Agriculture field investigators — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(7)
Funeral home directors and employees; coroners; medical examiners — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(8)
Any member of the clergy — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(9)
Medical, nursing, social work and counseling personnel of any office or clinic that provides abortions, abortion referrals, or contraceptives — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(10)
reporting_details: Illinois is not a universal-reporting state: only the professionals listed in 325 ILCS 5/4(a) must report, any other person may report voluntarily under 325 ILCS 5/4(f), and every report goes to the single statewide DCFS hotline required by 325 ILCS 5/7.6 (1-800-25-ABUSE / 1-800-252-2873).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 24 hours; immediately, regardless of the time of day or night, if the child's immediate safety or well-being is endangered or the family may flee (325 ILCS 5/7.4(b)(2))
60 days to determine "indicated" or "unfounded"; extendable in additional periods of up to 30 days for good cause (325 ILCS 5/7.12)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Report may be deemed "undetermined" where a complete investigation was not possible (325 ILCS 5/7.12)
